analyzed_vuln.description: get_coffset() calls blosc2_getitem() on the compressed offsets chunk and only checks rc < 0 and *offset > frame->len. It does not validate that exactly one int64_t item was returned (rc == sizeof(int64_t)) before using *offset. With malformed frame data, blosc2_getitem/_blosc_getitem can return a short positive byte count, leaving offset partially/uninitialized. That corrupted offset is then used to build/read a lazy chunk, feeding invalid chunk metadata into decompression and eventually causing blosc_d() to compute a negative neblock that is cast to unsigned in memset (negative-size-param).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In decompress_frame_fuzzer, attacker-controlled input is parsed as an in-memory frame via blosc2_schunk_from_buffer, then blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk -> frame_decompress_chunk -> frame_get_lazychunk -> get_coffset is reached. A crafted offsets chunk that makes blosc2_getitem return a non-negative but short/incomplete result for one int64 offset triggers use of an invalid offset. Subsequent lazy-chunk/header interpretation yields inconsistent block/chunk sizes so blosc_d performs memset with a huge unsigned size derived from negative neblock, crashing under ASan.
